---
title: "Recruit the Beast"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** You will install Claude Code, confirm it works, and start it in a throwaway folder in plan mode.
- **Before you start:** [Save Point](../crypt/shield-of-undo.html); a terminal (macOS, Linux, or WSL 2, the Windows Subsystem for Linux, on Windows); internet; and a Claude Team plan login or an Anthropic API key. An API key gives programmatic access to the models, billed per token; a plan is a subscription with usage limits.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes. Nothing here edits your files.
:::

Claude Code is strong, so you start it on a short lead before it does anything.

## 1. Install

On macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux, or inside a WSL 2 terminal, run the native installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, install inside WSL 2 and use the Linux command there. Check the result:

```bash
claude --version     # prints a version number
claude doctor        # read-only diagnostics; changes nothing
```

If the shell says `command not found`, the launcher lives in `~/.local/bin/claude` and that folder is not on your `PATH`.

## 2. Log in

Run `claude` and a browser opens. With a Team plan, log in with the account your admin invited you to. With an API key, `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...` instead.

::: {.callout-note}
If you have both a subscription login and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the key is used once you approve it, so usage goes to the API account. Run `/status` (a `/command` is typed inside the running tool) to see which login is active. Run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` if you did not mean to use the key.
:::

## 3. Start on a short lead

Make a throwaway folder and start in **plan mode**. It reads files, runs read-only commands and leaves your source untouched:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/odyssey-scratch && cd ~/odyssey-scratch
claude --permission-mode plan
```

`Shift+Tab` cycles `default`, `acceptEdits` and `plan` inside a session; the status bar shows the current mode.

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `default` | asks the first time each tool is used |
| `acceptEdits` | auto-accepts file edits and common file commands (`mkdir`, `touch`, `mv`, `cp`) in the working directory |
| `plan` | reads and runs read-only commands; leaves source files untouched |
| `bypassPermissions` | skips prompts; use only in containers or VMs |

## 4. Check the setup

Two commands share the name *doctor*.

- **`claude doctor`** runs in the shell. It prints read-only diagnostics of your installation and settings without starting a session, so use it when `claude` will not start.
- **`/doctor`** (alias `/checkup`) runs inside a session as a bundled skill, a ready-made skill that ships inside the tool. It reports first and changes something only after you confirm. It looks at installation health, extensions and their context cost, instruction files, permissions and usage.

### Which command shows what

| Command | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `/status` | version, model, account, connectivity, and which settings sources are active |
| `/context` (`/context all` expands it) | context use by category, with optimisation suggestions and warnings |
| `/usage` | session cost and plan limits |
| `/memory` | your `CLAUDE.md` files and auto memory, editable |
| `/mcp` | MCP servers (tool plug-ins) and their connection status |
| `/permissions` | allow, ask and deny rules by scope |
| `/hooks` | configured hooks, grouped by event |
| `/skills` | the skills available; press `t` to sort by token count |
| `/skill-doctor` | per-skill context cost and how often each is used |
| `/doctor` | setup checkup: report first, fixes only after you confirm |
| `claude doctor` | read-only install and settings diagnostics from the shell |
| `claude --debug` | debug logging; logs go to `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt` |

OpenCode has `opencode debug paths`, which prints where its files live.

### Before you ask for help

A bug report includes your OS, the install command and the full error output. `/feedback` sends feedback from inside a session. If you are unsure which problem applies, run `/doctor` or `claude doctor` to narrow it down. Read any output before you paste it into a bug report or chat, because it can contain paths and account details.
